description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself. Closed out 2026-05-08; substrate-convergence work in analyses 026-030 + the Geocities showcase landed the "Tweedles don't ship" bug class. P7 evals deferred behind P8 (operator interface) so the eval harness has a usable surface to run against.

phases.title: Observer API
phases.notes: HistoricalRunHandle reads any captured snapshot directory — parses run.log, reads the per-agent SQLite databases, loads the telemetry JSON, exposes summary() / meetings() / utterances() / per_agent_telemetry() / artifacts(). The replay-side surface that everything else in P8 sits on. Shipped 2026-05-07 alongside P8.2.

phases.title: TUI Inspector
phases.notes: Textual-based read-only TUI: snapshot library, run summary, meeting detail with body preview + speaker filter + utterance modal, artifact browser (global + meeting-scoped, attribution via bus not mtime), cast view, theme cycling, app-wide vim navigation. First public release — wonderland-ai 0.0.1 on PyPI 2026-05-08.

phases.title: Streaming + Mock Turtle
phases.notes: Foundation for live-watch UX. Extend RunHandle with stream_events() async iterator; HistoricalRunHandle defaults to yield-now (no behavior change for inspector); MockTurtleHandle replays a snapshot's events with compressed timing + dwell cap so we iterate live-watch UI against a free testbed. After P8.3 the TUI can subscribe to "events as they arrive" without caring whether the source is replay, mock, or eventually a real bus.

phases.title: Live-watch screen
phases.notes: New LiveRunScreen that consumes the streaming API — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator, live cost ticker, drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay so zero API spend during UX iteration. The screen that turns Wonderland from "things happen and you read transcripts later" into "things happen and you watch them happen."

phases.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
phases.notes: NewRunScreen — directive textarea, workflow picker (TDD/canonical/smoke), project-root picker. LiveRunHandle wraps a real Runner+Caucus, emits via the same streaming API as MockTurtleHandle so the live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably. The leap from "replay testbed" to "actually launches a real run." First end-to-end test: directive → live watch → artifacts → done.

phases.title: New-project spinup (the rabbit hole)
phases.notes: Three entry paths converging on a single project-context capture: greenfield (skeleton picker + scaffold), existing-Wonderland (already covered by P8.5's project picker), adopt-existing (wonderland init + stack-detection routine that pre-fills the context form from manifest files). Persists .wonderland/project-context.md in a forward-compatible shape so future workflow-context injection has one input format to read. The on-ramp that turns "pip install" into "team's ready to start."

phases.title: First-use polish
phases.notes: Welcome/home screen (new run / browse snapshots / cast / configure), error states (missing API key, no project root, run failure), abort flow (clean shutdown of running threads), quiescence indicator (M5's long pauses need "still working, just thinking"), README + SHOWCASE updates with the TUI flow. The rough-edges sweep that closes the gap between "works for the developer" and "works for someone who just installed it."

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

phases.title: Meeting turns: phases + priority + rotations
phases.notes: Per analysis 033 (analyses/033-meeting-as-mtg-turn.md): lift phases + priority rotation + turns-as-budget from MtG into the meeting engine; skip the stack. Sequenced as a substrate phase that alternates with P8's interface track per the back-and-forth-stays-fresh rhythm. Engine work is bigger than P8's per-task shape and benefits from its own phase boundary. Engine + workflow schema + observer events are P1 (load-bearing); rotation counter + failure-mode detectors are P2 (instrumentation that lands once the structure exists).

phases.title: Two-Headed Giant: team windows
phases.notes: Per the live r35-tdd-serial-phased observation: strict-serial priority within a rotation imposes ~N× cast size wall-clock cost on constitutionally-paired agents (Tweedledee/Tweedledum, Alice/Hatter) who in legacy mode would have deliberated concurrently. Phase 9.5 generalizes phases by adding team_groupings: list[list[str]] per phase. A team window opens concurrently for all team members via asyncio.gather; structural cap preserved (rotation budget × team count = bounded deliberations); §VIII observability preserved (per-agent WindowOutcome unchanged). Maps onto MtG's Two-Headed Giant format — paired players take their team turn together. The natural design follow-up to P9; lands once analysis 034 quantifies the wall-clock penalty of the strict-serial baseline.

phases.title: Cost recovery: tool-call surfacing + diff-based writes
phases.notes: Per analyses 032 + 035: Tweedles are 78.8% of total run cost, with ~13-15 calls per deliberation reflecting heavy write_file → run_tests → write_file tool loops. Two batched fixes: (1) surface tool calls on the bus event log so post-run analysis can quantify exactly which tool calls drive cost (currently inferred via per-agent telemetry); (2) diff-based write tool that lets agents send deltas instead of full file contents, with analysis 032 estimating ~3.5× cost compression on iterative file authoring. Sequencing: surface first so we can measure baseline tool-call distribution; then diff tool with measurements to verify the predicted compression. After both ship, second pass to identify other easy cost/clock wins from whatever the surfaced data reveals.

phases.title: Polish: ambient liveness, first-use UX, small ergonomic improvements after P11
Feature lifecycle + workflow composability: split design / implement / verify; operator batching

activePhase.title: Polish: ambient liveness, first-use UX, small ergonomic improvements after P11
activePhase.goal: P11 shipped projects as a first-class abstraction with full dashboard. Polish covers the ergonomic + ambient-liveness layer on top: things that don't add capability but make the substrate pleasant to live in. Subsumes the unrealized 'first-use polish' goal of p8.7 (which was queued before projects existed; with the project library as the new home, first-use UX is implicitly designed around 'create your first project'). Does not block P12 architecture work; can ship in pieces alongside other phases.
activePhase.sequencing: T84 (chase animation on Meetings pane) opens the phase as a small load-bearing UX win — doubles as a stuck-detector for live runs (frozen border = no utterances landing, complement to Dodo's nudge ladder). Subsequent tasks file as they surface; polish phase grows organically rather than being scoped up-front.

tasks.title: Chase animation on Meetings pane border (active-meeting indicator + stuck-detector)
tasks.details:
Animate small Unicode emotes around the perimeter of the active meeting's container in the live-watch view. Doubles as: (a) a passive 'which meeting is active' affordance distinct from cursor-selection, (b) a stuck-detector — when no utterances are landing, the chase pauses; operator can glance at the screen and see 'we're frozen' without waiting for Dodo's nudge ladder to fire.

Mechanics:
- Reactive _chase_position: int on the active meeting widget; advances on each AgentActEvent landing (not on a wall-clock tick — pace ties to actual signal so idle = no movement)
- set_interval at low rate (200-500ms) just to refresh()
- Position math: n_steps = 2*(width + height) - 4; position % n_steps maps back to (x, y) on the perimeter
- Implementation likely a small Static widget overlaid via dock + offset, or a custom render pass that swaps a single perimeter character for the emote

Cast pairings to wire (default + per-meeting variants):
- Default / no specific pairing: Alice 🌻 chasing the White Rabbit 🐇
- M2.5 (composition): just the Rabbit 🐇 alone — emphasize the meeting that loves to fail (analysis 039)
- M4 (test scenarios): Mad Hatter 🎩 dropping behind the Tweedles 👯
- M6 (review): Cheshire Cat 😼 fading in/out alongside Caterpillar 🐛
- Stuck state (no movement past N seconds): emote dims / static color shift to signal 'frozen'

Polish dimensions to settle while implementing:
- Emoji rendering varies wildly across terminals; need an ASCII fallback (e.g. 'A' → 'R' chase) for terminals that render emoji as boxes. Settings toggle: animation off / ASCII / emoji.
- Tick rate vs. activity rate: too fast = distracting, too slow = doesn't feel alive. Calibrate against r40-style runs (~20 utterances/min average).
- Color: should track theme tokens so theme switches don't break the visual.

Diagnostic value framing: this is decoration that earns its keep by giving operators a passive ambient signal of liveness. Frozen border = the substrate's softest stuck-detector, complementary to (not replacing) Dodo's escalation ladder.
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/tui/widgets/chase.py — ChaseStrip widget mounted in LiveRunScreen between the Meetings label and the meetings DataTable. Alice ('a') chasing the White Rabbit ('R') along a 28-char track of '·' dots. Rabbit moves every tick; Alice every other tick (gap oscillates, chase never resolves — Alice never catches Rabbit). Tick fires on each UtteranceEmitted or AgentActed event flowing through LiveRunScreen, so motion ties to actual signal-of-life. _check_idle runs every 2s and adds .-idle class when no tick fired in IDLE_THRESHOLD_SECS (15s default); CSS dims the row when stale. Single-cell ASCII characters for terminal-width safety; emoji upgrade easy if needed. 11 tests: starting frame, render-track shape, tick-advance semantics for both characters, wrap-around, reset, idle dim/clear behavior, integration with LiveRunScreen mount.

tasks.title: Feature lifecycle data layer + persistence
tasks.details: FeatureState enum (proposed, in_design, designed, queued, in_progress, ready_for_review, verified, rejected) + per-project state registry (.wonderland/feature-states.jsonl, append-only state-transition log). Each transition records: feature_slug, from_state, to_state, by (agent_name or 'operator'), at (timestamp), notes (optional). API: get_state(slug), list_features_in_state(state), transition(slug, to_state, by, notes). Synthesize state-transition utterances on the bus so cross-run continuity (analysis 039 fix) carries lifecycle state forward. Frozen artifact pattern preserved — feature payload itself stays immutable; state lives in the registry, not the artifact.

tasks.title: Workflow input filter: seed only features in state X
tasks.details: New workflow YAML field: meeting.input_filter (or workflow-level pre-meeting filter). When set, seed resolution drops features whose lifecycle state isn't in the filter's allowed set. Default: no filter (current behavior — all features visible). Used by tdd-implement to scope M5 iterations to features in 'queued' state. Composable with the existing per_item iteration: filter first, then iterate.

tasks.title: Workflow output transitions: features X→Y on phase complete
tasks.details: Workflow YAML gains meeting.on_complete_transition: {features_with_artifact: kind, from_state: X, to_state: Y}. After meeting completes successfully, features with the named artifact kind get auto-transitioned. E.g. tdd-design's M4 transitions features with test_scenario artifacts from in_design → designed. Implementation workflow's M6 transitions features with approved review from in_progress → ready_for_review. Layered fail-loud: if expected artifact didn't ship, transition is skipped + warning logged.

tasks.title: Split tdd-serial-phased into tdd-design + tdd-implement workflows
tasks.details:
Author two new workflows in closet/workflows/:
- tdd-design.yaml: M1 (scoping) + M2 (decomposition) + M2.5 (composition) + M3 (contract-negotiation) + M4 (test-scenarios). Output: features in 'designed' state. No M5, no M6.
- tdd-implement.yaml: M5 (implementation, per_item over queued features) + M6 (review, per_item). Input filter: features must be in 'queued' state. Output transition: in_progress → ready_for_review.
Keep tdd-serial-phased as the all-in-one for operators who want a single end-to-end run; tdd-design + tdd-implement are the composable atoms. Tests cover: design workflow produces designed-state features; implement workflow scoped to queued features only; combined design→implement→review flow ships verified features.

tasks.title: Features tab in project dashboard with state badges + batch-select
tasks.details: 5th tab in ProjectDashboardScreen (Runs / Artifacts / Files / Metrics / Features). Two-pane: features list left (one row per feature with state badge — color-coded: gray=proposed, blue=in_design, cyan=designed, yellow=queued, magenta=in_progress, green=ready_for_review, bright_green=verified, red=rejected), feature dossier right (story refs, ticket refs, contracts, scenarios, implementation notes if present, review verdict if present). Multi-select via space (lazygit pattern); 'q' (or another key) batch-queues selected features for the next implement run; 'v'/'r' marks verified/rejected when state is ready_for_review.

tasks.title: Operator verify/reject UI with notes
tasks.details: Modal on Features tab: 'v' on a feature in ready_for_review state opens a verification dialog. Shows feature dossier + 'Verified / Rejected / Cancel'. Rejection prompts for notes (required). Notes get stored in the state-transition log AND emitted as state_change utterance with the rejection text — flows into next run's seed via T85's bus integration. Verified state also accepts optional notes (positive feedback for the team). Notes feed Alice and Caterpillar on the next iteration.

tasks.title: Auto-transition rules (proposed→in_progress, in_progress→ready_for_review)
tasks.details:
Background watcher that auto-transitions features based on artifact presence:
- proposed → in_progress: first implementation artifact lands referencing the feature_slug
- in_progress → ready_for_review: ALL of (every ticket in feature has implementation, run_tests passes for feature's test files, M6 verdict for feature is 'approve')
No auto-transition past ready_for_review — that requires operator. Implementation: a runtime hook that fires on each implementation/review utterance and re-evaluates the feature's transition eligibility. Layers on top of T87's explicit workflow-level transitions (T87 = end-of-phase, T91 = real-time per-utterance).
